title: Odrysian Kingdom
capsule: The Odrysian Kingdom was the first and most powerful unified Thracian state, founded by Teres I around 480 BCE and reaching its apex under Sitalces (r. c. 431–424 BCE), who led an army of 150,000 men into Macedonia in 429 BCE in alliance with Athens — the campaign described at length by Thucydides. The kingdom controlled a wide arc from the Danube delta to the Aegean coast and extracted tribute from Greek coastal cities, but it fragmented repeatedly among rival Odrysian princes. Philip II of Macedon reduced Thrace to a client state by 341 BCE, and the date of 337 BCE in the batch data marks the effective end of Odrysian independence under Macedonian hegemony.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The outer limits of Odrysian territory are attested by Thucydides and later Attic inscriptions recording tribute, but the precise internal frontiers fluctuated greatly with dynastic divisions and are reconstructed only approximately from numismatic and epigraphic evidence.
